title: Cherry Clafoutis
subtitle: Baked French custard pudding with cherries
excerpt: Fresh cherries baked in a lightly sweetened pancake batter until puffed and golden. A simple, elegant French dessert that is halfway between a custard and a pudding.

recipe.sourceNotes: Clafoutis is a traditional baked dessert from the Limousin region of France. The original version uses unpitted cherries: the stones are said to release a subtle almond flavour during baking, though most recipes now stone the cherries for ease of eating. The batter is a thin, crêpe-like mixture of flour, eggs, and milk that puffs up in the oven around the fruit and sets into a custardy texture. The dish falls as it cools, which is expected and not a failure. Other stone fruits work well: prune plums, apricots, and peaches are all traditional in France.

content.text: Butter the dish generously and let it warm in the oven before adding the batter: this creates a lightly crisped base. The batter is very thin, thinner than a pancake batter. Rest it for 30 minutes if possible, or make it the night before and refrigerate it. The clafoutis is done when the edges are set and puffed and the centre is just firm with only a slight wobble.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Generously butter a 25 cm oven-proof ceramic dish. Dust with caster sugar. Place in the oven to warm while you make the batter.
Whisk together the eggs and sugar until combined. Whisk in the flour, then gradually whisk in the milk and cream. Add the vanilla. The batter will be thin.
Scatter the cherries in the warmed dish. Pour the batter over. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until puffed and golden and the centre is just set. Dust generously with icing sugar and serve warm.
